# ebook2cwgui

**Graphical front end for ebook2cw**

- **Version recorded:** 0.1.2
- **Categories:** `cw`, `morse-training`
- **Upstream:** <https://fkurz.net/ham/ebook2cw.html#gui>
- **Needs first:** `ebook2cw`

## What it does

Puts a wxWidgets window around ebook2cw: pick a text file, set character speed, effective speed, pitch and output format, and press the button. It runs the same converter and produces the same files.

## Why you would want it

The command-line tool has around twenty options and the two that matter most — character speed and effective speed — are easy to confuse. Seeing them as two labelled boxes side by side is worth more than it sounds when you are setting up a practice regime you intend to keep.

## Before it will work

ebook2cw itself, which this manifest declares as a dependency. A desktop session; it is a GUI and has no command-line mode.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`morse`](../profiles/morse.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install ebook2cwgui --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `ebook2cwgui`

## Known problems

It is a thin wrapper and does not expose every ebook2cw option. For anything beyond speed, pitch and format — chapter splitting patterns, frequency shifts between chapters, ID3 detail — use ebook2cw directly.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
